messages:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-choice change (selector v2) we see a ~3–4% increase in p99 token latency for /v1/generate on prod-dedicated. Grafana token-latency-by-kernel panel spiked at ~02:12 UTC. SM occupancy jumped ~12%, per-GPU VRAM per-container +~300MB, and MIG slice usage looks skewed :eyes:. Attaching quick profiling summary below.

perf-bot: alert: latency_regression detected route=/v1/generate p99 +4.1% at 2026-03-17T02:12Z, source=canary->prod rollout

chris: can you paste the grafana / prom queries you used? any kernel fallback churn in logs?

alex: quick queries I ran:
```
# token rate by kernel
sum by(kernel) (rate(tokens_generated_total[5m]))

# p99 token latency by route+kernel
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, kernel))

# kv cache evictions
increase(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool="ngen"}[10m])
```
Kernel selector picked `matmul-fused-v3` for many sequences >512. Fallbacks were low, but memory pattern looks worse.

maya: did the batcher config change in the same deploy? I remember a small tweak to max_batch_ms -> 8ms last week. Could be interacting.

sanjay: If occupancy is higher but latency also higher, my hunch is memory access pattern + VRAM pressure (more async copies?) -> more KV evictions. Check `kv_cache_hit_ratio` and `kv_prefetch_*` metrics. Prefetch windows that are too eager can bloat VRAM.

alex: kv stats: `kv_cache_hit_ratio` dropped ~2.6% over the window and `increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[10m])` = 420 (baseline ~40). So huge bump. Prefetch ops spiked in same minute.

linda: I'll add a dashboard panel: "kv-prefetch vs token tail-latency" and a per-GPU MIG-slice heatmap with occupancy, VRAM usage, and power draw. Assigning to myself, ETA 48h. :+1:

chris: mitigation options now: 1) rollback selector-v2 rollout for route /v1/generate (fast) 2) reduce prefetch window / lower prefetch concurrency 3) temporary batcher cap (reduce max batch size for affected route). Rollback command (runbook):
```
./deploy rollback --component=kernel-selector --version=selector-v1 --env=prod --route=/v1/generate
```
Do we want to rollback immediately?

alex: I'm kicking a targeted rollback on 3 GPUs in cluster-prod-ngen (canary subset) now. Will watch p99 and kv metrics. Running: `./deploy status --id=rb-176543`.

perf-bot: alert: rollback_action_started id=rb-176543 user=alex

(alex after 7m): Rollback applied to canary subset. p99 trending back down toward baseline, kv evictions dropping. Monitoring further.

perf-bot: alert resolved: latency_regression route=/v1/generate p99 returned to baseline after rollback (2026-03-17T02:22Z)

maya: thanks. Follow-up asks: we need better instrumentation to correlate kernel_choice + batch_size_at_dispatch + kv_prefetch footprint per-request. Right now those are in separate dashboards so root cause takes too long. Propose adding trace tags: `kernel_choice`, `batch_size_at_dispatch`, `kv_prefetch_count` and a router-level metric `last_chosen_kernel`.

sanjay: +1. I'll draft a short RFC to add those runtime tags and metric exports. I can own the runtime changes (small) and perf team will own dashboard panels. Link to RFC draft: https://go/repo/rfc/kernel-metrics (placeholder).

linda: I'll open a dashboard PR with the kv-prefetch panel, a kernel-choice histogram per-route, and a MIG slice occupancy heatmap. Also add an alert: kv_evictions > 100/min AND p99_delta > 2% => auto rollback suggestion.

alex: closing loop: we'll run an offline perf matrix across kernels × seq_len buckets + batch_size ranges to catch cases where a kernel looks better on throughput but harms token tail-latency due to memory behavior. I'll upload results to the perf drive and link here. Thanks folks. :pray:
